stages.title: Workshop Setup & Cover Information
stages.purpose: Identify the workshop: what it is called, under which scheme and sanction, for which craft and cluster, where and when it runs, and who is responsible for it. These fields become the cover page of every report generated from this record.

fields.label: Workshop title
fields.help: As written on the sanction order, e.g. “Design & Prototype Development Workshop — Sambalpuri Ikat”.

fields.label: Scheme
fields.help: The scheme funding the workshop, e.g. National Handicrafts Development Programme.

fields.label: Craft
fields.help: Filled in from the linked record when one is chosen. It is stored on this entry as well as the link, so the report still prints it if that record is later changed or removed.

fields.label: Craft name in the local language
fields.help: Written in the local script. It is printed in the report exactly as typed. Filled in from the linked record when one is chosen. It is stored on this entry as well as the link, so the report still prints it if that record is later changed or removed.

fields.label: Linked craft record
fields.help: Choose the craft from the crafts already documented. The cover fields above are filled in from it.

fields.label: Duration
fields.help: Leave blank to derive it from the start and end dates.

fields.label: Workshop ID
fields.help: The implementing agency’s own reference for this workshop.

fields.label: Venue location
fields.help: Captured from the device once, at the venue.

fields.label: Cover photograph
fields.help: Printed large on the cover page of the report.

stages.title: Introduction & Administrative Documentation
stages.purpose: The prose that opens the report: why the workshop was held, who supported it, what it set out to deliver. Written once and reused across the agency's reports.
stages.notes: Reviewer marked the Advanced tier of this stage as “Phase 2 work”.

fields.label: Acknowledgement
fields.help: Whom the workshop thanks: the sanctioning office, the cluster, the artisans.

fields.label: Programme objectives
fields.help: One objective per line.

fields.label: Expected deliverables
fields.help: One deliverable per line.

stages.title: Workshop Plan, Participants & Opening
stages.purpose: The day-by-day plan, the artisans who took part, the designer's own profile, and the record of the opening session.
stages.notes: The reviewer marked the Standard tier of this stage “Important for us”.

fields.label: Officials present at the opening
fields.help: One official per line, with designation.

fields.label: Artisans enrolled
fields.help: Leave blank to count the participant list below.

fields.label: Session
fields.help: Forenoon, afternoon, full day.

fields.label: Artisan record

stages.title: Cluster, Area & Craft Background
stages.purpose: The setting: where the cluster is, how the craft is practised there, what it has traditionally made, and what the community's dependence on it looks like.
stages.notes: The reviewer noted that traditional and contemporary DESIGNS belong to the next section, not here, and that several Standard-tier items should be optional. Both are reflected: this stage carries motifs, forms and colours as craft vocabulary, while design direction sits in stage 10.

fields.label: Traditional products
fields.help: One product per line.

fields.label: Access & connectivity
fields.help: Nearest road, rail and town; how the cluster is reached.

fields.label: Livelihood dependence on the craft
fields.help: What share of household income the craft provides, and for how many.

fields.label: Local terminology
fields.help: Craft terms in the local language, with their meaning.

stages.title: Traditional Process, Tools & Raw Materials
stages.purpose: The craft as it is practised before the workshop intervenes: the sequence of making, the tools, the materials and where they come from, and the problems the artisans already name.
stages.notes: The reviewer noted that stages 5 and 6 “may come later when they actually go to the field after market and consumer survey”, so this stage is completable out of order.

fields.label: Broad process steps
fields.help: The making sequence in outline. Individual steps are recorded below.

fields.label: Current problems
fields.help: One problem per line.

fields.label: Quality indicators
fields.help: How the artisans themselves judge a good piece.

fields.label: Documented process
fields.help: Choose a process already documented for this workshop instead of re-describing it.

fields.label: Step name
fields.help: Filled in from the linked record when one is chosen. It is stored on this entry as well as the link, so the report still prints it if that record is later changed or removed.

fields.label: Documented tool
fields.help: Choose a tool already documented anywhere in the repository. Its details are filled in below and can be corrected on this row.

fields.label: Tool
fields.help: Filled in from the linked record when one is chosen. It is stored on this entry as well as the link, so the report still prints it if that record is later changed or removed.

fields.label: Local name
fields.help: Filled in from the linked record when one is chosen. It is stored on this entry as well as the link, so the report still prints it if that record is later changed or removed.

fields.label: Type
fields.help: What kind of tool this is, in the words the artisans use. Choose the family below as well, so the same tool can be counted across clusters.

fields.label: Tool family
fields.help: The broad category, for counting tools across workshops. Describe the tool itself in “Type” above.

fields.label: Used for

fields.label: Source
fields.help: Where the material is bought or gathered.

fields.label: Cost per

stages.notes: Completable out of order, with stage 5. The Advanced tier's 360-degree capture and automated quality assessment were marked by the reviewer as a later plug-in; the multi-view photograph slots that such a feature would consume are captured here.

stages.title: Market Survey Planning
stages.purpose: What the survey is meant to find out, who will be asked, where, and with which questions.
stages.notes: The reviewer suggested the Advanced tier here be “a simple upload tool and phase 2 work”.

fields.label: Survey objectives
fields.help: One objective per line.

fields.label: Questionnaire
fields.help: The questions to be asked. One per line.

fields.label: Questionnaire languages
fields.help: Languages the questionnaire was translated into.

fields.label: Type
fields.help: What the place is, as it is known locally. Choose the channel below as well, so places can be compared across surveys.

fields.label: Market channel
fields.help: Which kind of outlet this place is. The same list the products and the buyer links use, so a survey can be compared with them.

stages.title: Market Survey & Field Data
stages.purpose: What the survey actually found: responses from each group, photographs of the market, prices seen, and the competing products on the shelf.
stages.notes: The reviewer asked for “a basic structure with text and image fields at the beginning. Later we can refine.” — which is what this stage is. Voice transcription and competitor image matching were deferred to “Phase 3 and only 1 or 2 features”.

stages.title: Market Analysis & Design Direction
stages.purpose: What the survey means: the SWOT, the price bands the market will bear, and the design opportunities that follow from the evidence.
stages.notes: The reviewer marked most Standard-tier items optional and deferred the AI-assisted Advanced tier to “Phase 3 and some of them by the AI team”.

fields.label: Main design opportunities
fields.help: One opportunity per line.

fields.label: Evidence
fields.help: Which survey response or observation supports this.

stages.title: Design Brief & Concept
stages.purpose: The designer's own statement of what will be made and why: the concept, the market it is for, and the material, colour and motif direction it will follow.
stages.notes: The reviewer marked the Standard tier “some of these and only as optional fields” and deferred the structured, evidence-generated brief to “phase 4”. This is also where traditional and contemporary DESIGN direction belongs, per the reviewer's note on stage 4.

fields.label: Traditional design reference
fields.help: The traditional designs this work draws on. Moved here from the cluster background at the reviewer’s request.

fields.label: Craft-integrity baseline
fields.help: What must not change if the piece is still to be this craft.

stages.title: Sketch Development
stages.purpose: The design sketches produced during the workshop, each with its intent.
stages.notes: The reviewer marked the Standard tier “optional fields” and noted the Advanced image-processing tier as “may be Deepika app for now”. The vector/line-art slots such a tool would fill are present; the processing itself is not claimed here.

fields.label: Version
fields.help: Increment when a sketch is redrawn rather than replaced, so the iteration history survives.

fields.label: Line art / vector file
fields.help: An SVG or vector export, if one was produced.

stages.title: Sketch Review & Shortlisting
stages.purpose: Which sketches go forward to prototyping, and on whose judgement — the artisans' and the master craftsperson's as much as the designer's.
stages.notes: The reviewer wrote “we may consider deleting this entire section for now”. It is kept but marked optional: a workshop that skips it is still complete, and no field here is required of the workshop as a whole. It is retained because the selection reason is the only record of WHY a design was dropped, which the research use of this data needs.

fields.label: Rank
fields.help: Where this sketch placed in a ranked review.

stages.title: Prototype Development
stages.purpose: The making of each prototype: who made it, from what, how long it took and what it cost, with the record of problems met along the way.
stages.notes: The reviewer wrote “let's simplify” on the Basic tier, and referred the Advanced measurement tier to “Kumarjit da and team”, noting “the system we used in the workshop app… we can supply a PDF of measurements to be printed”.

fields.label: Artisan assigned
fields.help: Chosen from the artisans enrolled at stage 3.

fields.label: Existing product developed from
fields.help: If this prototype reworks a product the artisan already makes, choose it here. The link is what lets the report show the before and the after.

fields.label: Developed from
fields.help: Filled in from the linked record when one is chosen. It is stored on this entry as well as the link, so the report still prints it if that record is later changed or removed.

fields.label: Measurement sheet
fields.help: A printable measured drawing, if one was produced.

fields.label: Amount
fields.help: Leave blank to compute it as quantity × rate.

stages.title: Prototype Iteration & Testing
stages.purpose: Every change made to a prototype after its first making, why it was made, and what it cost in time and money.
stages.notes: The reviewer marked the Standard tier “optional fields”.

fields.label: Problem type
fields.help: What went wrong, in your own words. Tick the areas below as well.

fields.label: Problem areas
fields.help: Tick every area the problem touched. More than one is normal.

stages.title: Prototype Selection & Validation
stages.purpose: Which prototypes were accepted, on what assessment, and with whose approval.
stages.notes: The reviewer marked the Standard tier “optional fields” and said of the Advanced tier “at the beginning — just crowdsourced designer feedback mechanism. Reset for Phase 4.”

fields.label: Quality checklist
fields.help: One check per line; prefix with ✓ or ✗.

stages.title: Final Product Documentation
stages.purpose: The catalogue record of each accepted product: its name and code, its final photographs, dimensions, materials, technique and description.
stages.notes: The reviewer referred the Advanced catalogue-asset tier to “Kumarjit plug in”.

fields.label: Product description
fields.help: The paragraph that would appear beside this piece in a catalogue.

stages.title: Costing, Packaging & Market Linkage
stages.purpose: What each product costs to make and what it should sell for, built from the line items rather than asserted, plus how it will reach a buyer.
stages.notes: The reviewer marked several Standard-tier items optional. The cost-calculator inputs are stored, not just the totals, so a figure in the report can always be traced to the quantities and rates it came from.

fields.label: Material cost
fields.help: The material total for this product — the Amount column of its material lines below, added up.

fields.label: Labour cost
fields.help: The labour total for this product — the Amount column of its labour lines below, added up.

fields.label: Total cost
fields.help: Derived from the costs above.

fields.label: Amount
fields.help: Derived as quantity × rate.

fields.label: Amount
fields.help: Derived as persons × days × rate.

stages.title: Workshop Outcomes, Problems & Feedback
stages.purpose: What the workshop achieved, what went wrong, and what the artisans and the designer say about it.
stages.notes: The counts here are derived from the records by default; the manual fields exist only to override a derived number, and an override carries a note explaining itself. The reviewer asked for “just option for voice and transcript — if you think it apt”, which is what the Advanced tier below is.

fields.label: Number of designs (override)
fields.help: Leave blank to count the sketches recorded.

fields.label: Number of prototypes (override)
fields.help: Leave blank to count the prototypes recorded.

fields.label: Reason for the override
fields.help: Required if either count above is filled in. It is printed under the headline figure, so it is what an officer reads beside the number.

stages.title: Inspection & Closing
stages.purpose: The closing session, the certificates issued and the inspecting officer's remarks.

fields.label: Signature
fields.help: Sign on the pad, or attach a photograph of the signed sheet. Attendance is recorded by the fields above and is never held up by this.

stages.title: Report Generation & Submission
stages.purpose: Choose the template, decide what the report contains, generate it, and keep a record of every file that was produced.
stages.notes: This stage configures the report rather than appearing in it, so no template prints it. Every export ever generated is recorded below, with its checksum, so a file submitted to an office can later be matched against the record it came from.

fields.label: Report colour
fields.help: Twelve colours chosen to stay distinguishable when the report is printed on a black-and-white office printer. Choose “Custom colour” to use the picker.

fields.label: Report colour (hex)
fields.help: The accent as #RRGGBB. Filled in for you when a named colour is chosen; the headings, the table headers, the rules and the figures are all derived from it. Left blank, the report keeps the template’s own colour.

fields.label: Report typeface
fields.help: Applies to the Word document, which is the file that is submitted and the one an officer edits. The PDF embeds whichever face the server has that can draw Odia, Devanagari and the rupee sign, so a typeface chosen here is reported as a warning rather than silently substituted there.

fields.label: Report title
fields.help: Leave blank to use the workshop title.

fields.label: Organisation line
fields.help: Printed above the title on the cover.

fields.label: Append the recordings’ transcripts
fields.help: Adds an annexure containing every transcript the workshop collected.

fields.label: Stages to leave out
fields.help: Stage keys omitted from this report.

fields.label: SHA-256
fields.help: Lets a submitted file be matched against this record.

fields.label: Generated on device
fields.help: True when the phone produced the file with no network.

stages.title: Data Quality & Archive
stages.purpose: Confirm that the record and its media are preserved, and record any quality problem found in the photographs before the record is archived.
stages.notes: Blur and resolution ARE computable on device — the variance of the Laplacian and the pixel dimensions — so those flags are real fields with an ``autoDetected`` marker rather than a deferred feature. Duplicate detection and search indexing are not claimed; the fields that would record their output are present.

stages.title: Post-Workshop Follow-up
stages.purpose: Whether the designs were actually taken up: what is being produced, what has sold, and what the artisans still need.
stages.notes: One record per product per monitoring interval, which is what makes design-survival analysis possible across workshops. Nothing here is required of the workshop itself — follow-up happens months later, and a workshop must be able to close without it.
